posts.title: T-day+1
posts.description: Crowds avoided. Christmas shopping almost done. Careful notes taken of what is going to whom, double checked so that I didn’t auto-fill anywhere to send to me instead of them. Amazon will not let me change the oops of HappyBirthdayMathias as the first name to MerryChristmasMathias (to signal that it’s not just another random Amazon box) and at the risk of losing the Black Friday price to time zone shenanigans, well, we definitely celebrate a birthday at Christmas, so I didn’t cancel it and start over. You make a mistake, I figure, grandmothers gotta grandmother. Now I just need to get to Andy’s Orchard to get some Blenheim apricot slabs for my mom’s 96th birthday.

posts.title: Turkey trip
posts.description: (What is up with the weird paragraph spacing.) There had been no plans to be here today. Michelle found a last-minute frozen 12 lb turkey, which we were told works without spending days thawing it if you cook it in a bag. Where did she put the bags. We looked everywhere. I walked away a minute and back just in time to see Richard, for I think the first time in his life, standing on a chair to see the back of the top shelf. *I* do that sort of thing all the time but I’m 15” shorter than he is. The chair slid, he fell, the radio broke, and the microwave lurched forward across the counter while I gasped, NO! I asked him never to do that again. He’s okay with that. But in catching himself on those he broke his fall, he assured me, and he was basically okay. Michelle’s friend rang the doorbell with some dairy-free pumpkin pie, which was so kind of her.
